title: Adaptive trip-score fallback policy for regional & tiered routing
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need an automated, low-latency fallback trigger that blends multiple operational signals (429s, timeouts, error rates, latency spikes, queue depth) into a single, interpretable "trip-score" per route+region+tier. The trip-score will drive three classes of actions: 1) soft fallbacks (route to a model variant or lower-cost tier), 2) regional cutovers (move traffic to alternative region), and 3) hard circuit trips (reject or throttle).

Background and motivation:
- Current fallback triggers are siloed (separate thresholds for 429s, timeouts, or p95 latency) and produce noisy flips during transient spikes.
- Product needs graceful degradation that respects customer SLOs, per-customer routing policies, and avoids cascading overload across regions.
- We want a single control plane primitive (trip-score) that operators and product can reason about, with tunable weights and hysteresis.

Goals and success metrics:
- Reduce P95/P99 SLO violations caused by overloaded pools by 30% under surge test.
- Keep false-positive fallback rate below 2% over a 24h window (false-positive = fallback when downstream capacity would have recovered without action).
- No more than 5% additional cost from fallback to higher-latency model variants during steady traffic.
- Provide per-route observability: trip-score timeseries, contributing signal breakdown, and action log.

High-level design:
1) Signals aggregated per (route, model_variant, region, tier) on two windows: short (1m) and medium (5m). Signals: 429_rate, timeout_rate, error_rate (5xx), p95_latency, queue_depth, active_requests.
2) Normalize each signal to a 0..1 risk band using running baseline percentiles per-region and per-tier. Normalization reduces sensitivity to regional traffic patterns.
3) Compute trip-score = sum_i (w_i * normalized_signal_i) where weights w_i are configurable per-route and default to {429:0.35, timeout:0.25, error:0.2, p95:0.15, queue:0.05}.
4) Hysteresis and decay: require trip-score > trip_threshold (default 0.65) on medium window to trigger fallback; require trip-score < recover_threshold (default 0.45) on short window for re-allow. Implement exponential decay cooldown to avoid flip-flopping (cooldown_min=30s, cooldown_max=5m).
5) Action matrix: depending on route policy and isolation level, map trip_score ranges to actions: 0.65-0.8 => model-variant fallback (quantized or smaller), 0.8-0.95 => regional reroute to same-tier in alternate region, >=0.95 => circuit trip and fail-fast with standardized 503 and troubleshooting guidance.
6) Per-customer overrides: customers on Dedicated/Private can pin to "no cross-region fallback" and instead take only model-variant fallbacks. Enterprise customers can supply custom weight profiles and thresholds.

Operational details and data model:
- Stats collection: lightweight counters emitted every 5s from each router worker and aggregated to a per-route Redis key (sharded). Keys are time-bucketed and TTL'd to 6m to cap memory.
- Scoring service: a stateless scorer reads aggregated counters, computes normalized signals, trip-score, and writes action decisions to a routing-config store (etcd) with revisioned timestamps.
- Rollout mechanism: scorer runs behind a feature flag (per-cluster) and publishes decisions as non-authoritative until enabled via gradual rollout. Router consults scoring decisions and applies action only if decision is authoritative for that cluster.
- Telemetry: new Grafana dashboards and Alerting rules for "trip-score spikes", "fallback rate", "fallback-latency delta", and "false-positive fallbacks". Logs include cause breakdown and resolution path.

Scoring formula (example):
- normalized_signal = clamp((value - baseline_p50) / (baseline_p95 - baseline_p50), 0, 1)
- trip_score = sum(weights * normalized_signal)
- Example: route /v1/chat in us-west0: 429_rate norm=0.8, timeout norm=0.1, p95 norm=0.5 => trip_score = 0.35*0.8 + 0.25*0.1 + 0.15*0.5 + ... = 0.347 -> below threshold (no action).

Trade-offs and discussion:
- Benefit: single interpretable number for operators and easier tuning per-route.
- Risk: score aggregation can obscure root cause (e.g., network vs model), mitigated by retaining signal breakdown in logs and dashboard.
- Complexity: introduces scorer service and Redis aggregation; mitigated by lightweight buckets and TTLs, and reuse of existing metric pipelines.
- Edge case: sustained low-volume but high-error customers may look noisy; add min-traffic floor before evaluation (min_active_requests=3).

Testing and validation plan:
- Unit tests for normalization, hysteresis and decay logic.
- Load tests: synthetic surge (spike RPS) and induced 429s via upstream rate limits to validate fallback selection and false-positive rate.
- Canary rollout: enable scorer as non-authoritative in canary region, compare decisions to baseline for 48h. If deviations within 1% of expected, promote to authoritative with 1% traffic, then 10%, then 50%.

Rollout and runbook:
1) Feature-flagged deploy of scorer and router changes (read-only decisions).
2) Canary run in ns-usw1 for 48h.
3) Gradual increase of authoritative traffic; monitor false-positive & SLO metrics.
4) If "trip-score spike" alerts > 5/min or false-positive > 2% for 1h, rollback scorer to non-authoritative.

Open questions & follow-ups:
- Should token-level partial completions be treated as separate signal? (concern from SRE about partials causing client retries).
- Evaluate cost impact of model-variant fallbacks under long tail traffic; add cost-budget guardrail to action matrix.
- Investigate offloading aggregation to the metric pipeline (Prometheus/Thanos) instead of Redis for scale.
